newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sees no budget impact from coal, construction.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sees no budget impact from coal, construction.

text.p: Thursday's agreement on coal subsidies and the 25 billion mark construction investment plan announced on Wednesday by Chancellor Helmut Kohl will not burden the government budget in 1997, the Finance Ministry said.

Spokesmen for the finance and economics ministries told Reuters the construction programme would be fully funded by the government-owned Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau and Deutsche Ausgleichsbank, and would have no impact on federal outlays.
The coal subsidies agreement will not start to affect the federal budget until 1998, raising spending by about 500 million marks from the current medium-term budget plan.

Budget data for 1997 will be decisive in determining the initial participants in European monetary union. To meet the EMU goals, Bonn is trying to reduce its deficit to three percent of gross domestic product.
